stories.title: Anthropic goes public on Nasdaq, debuting up sharply from its IPO price
stories.summary: Anthropic began trading on Nasdaq under ticker ANT at $111.50 a share, up from an $83 IPO price, valuing the company around $1.5 trillion in one of the largest tech IPOs on record.
stories.more: TechCrunch reports the stock traded as much as 33% above the IPO price and that the $83 IPO price raised more than $80 billion in new capital. The IPO reportedly delivered large personal payouts too: TechCrunch says Anthropic's seven co-founders each cashed out roughly $280 million, about $2 billion combined, while separately reporting the company's Public Benefit Foundation, employee donations, and company match could together deliver as much as $156 billion to charity at a $95 share price. Reuters, via Hacker News, frames the debut as a test of AI's promise and peril on Wall Street. The listing follows Anthropic's S-1 filing roughly a month earlier revealing its plans to go public.

stories.title: WeVisForensics proposes a self-evolving agent for detecting AI-generated video
stories.summary: A new paper introduces WeVisForensics, an agent system for spotting AI-generated video forgeries that evolves its own investigation strategy instead of using a fixed forensic pipeline.
stories.more: The paper argues that current AI video forensics tools fall short because they either reason in a single pass and miss brief or localized artifacts, or follow predefined multi-agent workflows with little flexibility in what they inspect. The authors note that making the investigation policy adaptive is not enough on its own, since it doesn't improve the forensic skill of the underlying fixed expert models. WeVisForensics is proposed as an alternative, though the excerpt cuts off before detailing exactly how the method works.

stories.title: VODA improves 3D Gaussian segmentation with volumetric supervision
stories.summary: Researchers propose VODA, a supervision method that uses local depth structure to fix weak training signals in 3D Gaussian Splatting segmentation.
stories.more: 3D Gaussian Splatting lets researchers segment and manipulate objects at the level of individual Gaussian primitives, but most segmentation methods are trained and evaluated only through rendered 2D views. The paper argues this mismatch lets models produce accurate-looking rendered masks even from incomplete 3D selections, because alpha-blended feature supervision concentrates learning on the Gaussians that dominate a view while leaving occluded or low-contribution ones weakly supervised. VODA is proposed as a plug-and-play objective that exploits local depth structure to address this, though the excerpt does not give further implementation or evaluation detail.

stories.more: The paper frames CAPTCHAs as a natural test of this loop, since humans solve them by clicking and dragging on screen and adjusting after seeing the result. The authors note that existing CAPTCHA benchmarks are largely already solved and rarely test spatial reasoning, while existing spatial benchmarks rarely require taking action. TuringSpace is introduced to address that gap, though the excerpt cuts off before detailing the benchmark's composition or results.

stories.title: LightTAR offers a lightweight, target-aware method for multimodal tabular learning
stories.summary: LightTAR is a new, inexpensive technique that adapts dimensionality reduction of text and image embeddings to better predict the target variable in multimodal tabular learning.
stories.more: Multimodal tabular learning combines structured numerical and categorical features with unstructured text and images, and these unstructured fields are typically represented using pretrained encoder embeddings reduced via PCA. The paper notes that PCA prioritizes variance in the data but can overlook information that is actually useful for predicting the target. LightTAR is introduced as a simple, low-cost method that adapts the dimensionality reduction step to be more target-aware, though the excerpt does not detail its exact mechanism or report benchmark results.

stories.title: WorldRuler targets interactive world models that follow custom gameplay rules
stories.summary: A new paper introduces WorldRuler, a framework for generative world models that follow user-defined rules for gameplay rather than only mimicking real-world physics.
stories.more: The authors note that different rules create distinct gameplay experiences even within similar scenes and action spaces, so customizable gameplay requires world models that can follow rules beyond realistic behavior. They identify two core challenges: preserving rule definitions, dependencies, and world state across saving and loading, and translating those rules into visual outcomes. The excerpt cuts off before describing WorldRuler's specific architecture or results.
